title: tenant policy inversion results in unexpected model downgrade and cross-region latency spike
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Customer reports started on 2025-02-09: a high-volume tenant observed sudden model downgrades (gptx-3 -> gptx-3-small) and routing to eu-west when configured region is us-west. The symptom included increased tail latency and degraded quality for production prompts. Preliminary investigation indicates tenant-scoped routing policy evaluation produced inverted priority ordering under specific config states, causing fallback logic to choose lower-tier variants in the wrong region.
reproduction_steps: 1) Use tenant T-918 with a mix of dedicated and hosted routes and an active canary rollout pinned to gptx-3
2) Simulate sustained steady traffic with occasional short bursts (Poisson 20qps baseline, 80qps bursts)
3) Apply a routing policy update that adds a temporary exclusion for a subset of GPUs (maintenance window)
4) Observe route selection logs in routing-service for sequence of decisions during policy-sync event
5) Verify requests are routed to gptx-3-small in eu-west instead of gptx-3 in us-west
impact_summary: Medium-to-High customer impact: one high-revenue tenant experienced degraded output quality and 2x tail latency for ~45 minutes across peak traffic. Several internal SLO alerts fired (latency p99 and error budget burn). No data exfiltration or security compromise observed.

root_cause: A race condition in the tenant-scoped policy merge routine during policy-sync allowed a recently-updated fallback priority list to be read before completion of index normalization. When index normalization lags, comparator logic that assumes strictly increasing priority indices can invert ordering for elements with transient index -1 markers. This led to selecting lower-tier model variants and cross-region fallthrough when local capacity flags were briefly unresolved.
fix_description: Primary fix: serialize policy normalization and comparator initialization during policy-sync to ensure no read of incomplete priority indices. Add a defensive check rejecting policy states containing placeholder indices (-1) with a retry backoff. Secondary fix: add explicit region affinity guard to prefer same-region variants unless capacity enforcement requires cross-region fallback.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge PR with comparator serialization and defensive checks into canary branch (engineering/routing-service)
2) Canary release to non-critical tenants (10% routing-traffic) for 2 hours
3) Monitor routing decision rates, p99 latency, and fallback counts; if stable, ramp to 50% then 100% over 6 hours
4) Coordinated config update to remove temporary explicit pinning for affected tenant once stable
5) Backport hotfix to dedicated and private branches and schedule private deployment patch notes
test_plan: Unit tests: comparator ordering under interleaved normalization sequences (add negative-index and out-of-order cases)
Integration tests: policy-sync with simulated index normalization delay and concurrent reads
Load tests: replay tenant traffic pattern with bursts to validate no inversion under high concurrency
Chaos test: simulate transient GPU capacity flags and verify region affinity guard triggers correct fallback
monitoring_signals: alerts: routing-inversion-detected (new synthetic alert based on comparator metrics)
